text:
mike: Heads-up — noticed a KV cache hit-rate drop from ~78% -> ~42% on canary after the system prompt change last night. CPU stayed flat but token latency increased. anyone on perf able to take a quick look?

tara: Hmm that's large. Did the change modify the system prompt text only or did we also add tool/function metadata to requests? :thinking:

mike: only the system prompt string changed (minor wording). No intentional tool metadata added. I attached a couple of perf samples from the trace.

jin: pinging tokenizer/runtime notes — small prompt changes can shift tokenization and prefix lengths, which breaks exact-match cache keying. are we hashing raw input bytes or token ids?

mike: we use a composite key: model+tokenizer_version+prefix_hash where prefix_hash = sha256(serialized_prompt). We hash the full prompt object (system + user + tool_context fields) serialized in insertion order.

sanjay: that explains it — any semantically irrelevant whitespace or trailing newline in system prompt will change the hash. we saw similar with 1769501234-era regressions. two levers: canonicalize prompt or relax keying to ignore system prompt for certain models.

eva: Suggestion: normalize by trimming, collapsing repeated whitespace, and normalizing Unicode NFKC. Also we should sort tool metadata keys before serialization. quick example: 

```json
// normalization pseudo
normalized = input.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').normalize('NFKC')
obj.tools = sortKeys(obj.tools)
key = sha256(JSON.stringify(obj))
```

jin: +1. Also pin tokenizer_version: if the tokenizer changes between deploys that can invalidate keys. We should include tokenizer checksum and only rotate it via an explicit migration.

tara: Another approach: make cache tiers. Tier 1 = prefix-only (system+first N tokens canonicalized) for hot-hit fast path. Tier 2 = full obj-hash. That gets us partial hits even when the system prompt tweaked.

mike: Tiered cache sounds promising. Do we have telemetry to estimate prefix-hit utility? I can run a sample over last 7 days traces to compute hit overlap between full-hash and prefix-hash.

infra-bot: deploy Canary-18325 started at 2026-03-16T09:12:30Z, hosts: canary-3/4.

sanjay: If we do prefix canonicalization, decide on N tokens or character length. Token-aware prefix is better (keeps semantics). But that needs tokenization at ingress — added overhead. Tradeoff: small CPU cost vs large hit-rate benefit.

eva: For warmup: spin a lightweight background warmup job that issues the top 500 unique prefixes observed in the past day to populate KV caches on boot. This avoids cold misses from model rollouts.

jin: For quick experiment: 1) implement simple whitespace/unicode canonicalization (no sorting) in the cache keyer, 2) pin tokenizer_version checksum in key metadata, 3) run a 6-hour A/B on canary with telemetry: hit-rate, p50/p95 token latency, cost.

tara: Also add a regression guard: if the canonicalizer reduces quality (measured by eval prompts or dets on our canary evals) we revert. We should run a small eval set to ensure no semantic collisions.

mike: I'll implement the normalization + tokenizer pin and run the A/B. I'll also produce a small script to compute overlap between canonicalized-prefix keys and the existing full-hash keys so we can estimate the hit uplift.

sanjay: For long-term: consider semantic-aware keying where we canonicalize function calls (normalize order, remove ephemeral ids) and keep stable placeholders for hidden tool fields.

eva: One more gotcha: streamed inputs (partial inputs) can produce different keys mid-request; ensure we only key on finalized prefix used by runtime caching.

mike: Action items: mike->proto normalization PR (tokenizer pin + whitespace+NFKC + tool-key sorting) by EOD. jin->generate tokenizer checksum utility. tara->define canary eval set. sanjay->prototype prefix warmup job. eva->add telemetry dashboard panels for prefix vs full hits.

tara: sounds good. if anyone hits blockers ping me. :thumbsup:

mike: I'll post follow-up with the A/B results and the sample overlap numbers. Thanks all. :eyes:
